messages:
Sam: getting multiple tickets from EU customers about slow first-byte times starting ~08:25 UTC. p95/p99 for TLS handshake jumped. Anyone on it?
Priya: yep, alert fired. Dashboard shows TLS handshake p99 up from ~120ms -> ~900ms in eu-central and eu-west between 08:24-08:40.
Marc: digging into edge logs + pcaps now. Early signs point to an odd path change — some traffic is getting hairpinned between POPs.
ingress-bot: detected route-flap via bgp-provider-3 at 08:26:47 :rotating_light:
Sam: customer repro (from a VM in eu-west):
```
curl -w "%{time_starttransfer}\n" -s -o /dev/null https://api.redwood-inference.example.com/v1/complete -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
traceroute -n -q1 api.redwood-inference.example.com
```
Marc: traceroute sample — notice the detour hop that adds ~200-400ms:
```
1  10.0.0.1  1.2 ms
2  52.11.22.33  5.6 ms
3  35.44.55.66  310.1 ms  <-- unexpected
4  52.22.33.44  312.3 ms
5  203.0.113.5  313.0 ms (edge)
```
oncall-sre: tcpdump at edge shows multiple SYN retransmits from upstream before we see client ClientHello forwarded, sample: 
```
08:27:15.100000 IP client > edge: Flags [S], seq 0
08:27:15.300123 IP client > edge: Flags [S] (retransmit)
08:27:15.600456 IP client > edge: Flags [S] (retransmit)
08:27:16.200789 IP edge > origin: Flags [S]
... TLS ClientHello arrives ~900ms after initial SYN
```
oncall-sre: packet loss / reordering on provider path looks likely.
Sam: DNS check? Could resolver be returning an Anycast address that sends some clients to a non-local POP?
Marc: authoritative A records unchanged; however some resolvers returned a different Anycast any-to-many mapping during the window, resulting in traffic landing in a provider POP that then tunnels to our eu POP in a different AZ (hairpin).
netops: confirmed with provider: they had a misapplied config on an upstream router that caused brief route withdrawals and path changes at 08:26-08:28. BGP flaps resulted in traffic moving via a backup peering in another AZ.
Sam: quick mitigations applied at 08:33 UTC:
- temporarily increased our POP preference for eu-west-local IP blocks (weight bump)
- added a short-lived static route to avoid the flaky transit (expire 1800s)
- adjusted edge keepalive and connection reuse to reduce number of new TLS handshakes
- added short timeout bump for backend idle to avoid mid-flight closes during extra RTTs
Marc: after those changes p95 returned to normal within ~3-5 minutes. p99 normalized shortly after.
Priya: created a short support note with repro steps + what we changed and posted to #support. support-bot notified customers with impacted keys.
fondu: noted a small rise in 502s during the hairpin window — looks like extra RTTs caused backend to hit upstream timeouts briefly.
Sam: action items / owners:
- NET-412: Provider RCA + request peer config hardening (owner: Marc)
- SRE-879: Add traceroute anomaly detector & alert (owner: Priya)
- SRE-880: Audit TLS session resumption rates; ensure session tickets not unusually low (owner: fondu)
- OPS-201: Add passive hairpin detection to edge metrics (owner: Sam)
oncall-sre: small runbook snippet added to oncall doc under "edge routing hairpin":
```
1) run traceroute from two EU vantage points
2) check bgp/bgp-providers dashboard for flaps
3) tcpdump at ingress to confirm retransmits
4) bump POP weight / add temporary static route
5) increase keepalive / reuse to reduce full handshakes
6) inform Support + customers
```
netops: provider has scheduled a maintenance to adjust BGP timers and prevent rapid flap oscillations. They will share logs and final RCA.
Priya: monitoring: we'll run synthetic requests every 60s from multiple EU probes for 48h and keep the alert threshold tighter for TLS handshake p99.
Sam: closing update: system stable, p95/p99 back in SLO. Leaving alerts on and follow-ups in Jira. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
support-bot: Posted to #support: "Heads-up: eu-region TLS handshake spike 08:24-08:40 UTC. Mitigations applied; monitoring ongoing. See NET-412 / SRE-879 for follow-ups."
